Each is two copies of the tree before it with one root hung under the other, so the size doubles from 2 to 4 to 8 nodes and the root gains one child per order." width="100%"} The binomial tree of order `0` is a single node, and the tree of order `k` is two copies of the tree of order `k - 1` with the root of one made a child of the root of the other. `B(k)` therefore has `2^k` nodes, its root has `k` children (which are the roots of `B(k-1)`, `B(k-2)`, ..., `B(0)`), and it has `C(k, d)` nodes at depth `d`, which is where the name comes from. Node numbering follows the construction: the first copy takes the first half of the numbers and the second copy the second half, so the root is the first node created and a node's parent is found by clearing the lowest set bit of its index (the numbering NetworkX's `binomial_tree()` uses). In a directed graph every edge points from parent to child. The tree is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Binomial trees are useful for: - illustrating binomial heaps, whose structure is a forest of binomial trees - modeling broadcast and gossip schemes in which every informed node informs one new node per round (the tree after `k` rounds is `B(k)`) - test cases for tree algorithms with an unbalanced but regular shape ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [order]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Order of the tree. Must be non-negative; `order=0` adds a single node. The tree has `2^order` nodes. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; the root gets the first number. A label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `order=` is negative. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} `B(3)` has `8` nodes, and its root has three children: ::: {#355f7513 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_binomial_tree(order=3) graph.count_nodes(), graph.get_out_degree("1") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (8, 3) ``` ::: ::: The number of nodes at each depth follows the binomial coefficients `1, 3, 3, 1`: ::: {#4d90f262 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} depths = graph.single_source_shortest_path_length("1", return_dict=True) [sum(1 for d in depths.values() if d == level) for level in range(4)] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [1, 3, 3, 1] ``` ::: :::
